title: Tuned Rating Systems Beat the Official RoboCore Score once Both Robots have Fought Before

detail.title: Tuned Rating Systems Beat the Official RoboCore Score once Both Robots have Fought Before

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author maintains tapout.gg, a public statistics site for RoboCore fights whose Elo rating (K = 32) is one of the baselines compared in this paper. The author declares no other competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable: the study uses publicly available competition results and involves no human participants.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific funding

detail.abstract: RoboCore runs robot competitions in Brazil and publishes an official score for every robot, yet 56% of its robots fought at a single event. We ask how well that score and three standard rating systems, Elo, Glicko-2 and TrueSkill, predict who wins the next fight using only earlier events. On 15,722 fights from 47 events (2013-2026), every rating system was tuned on events up to 2022 and scored on the 9,492 fights of 2023-2026. Read as an Elo win probability, the official score picks the winner of 60.3% of fights with a mean log-loss (lower is better) of 0.659 nats, against 0.693 for a coin flip. Glicko-2 lowers the log-loss by 0.0061 (95% event-bootstrap interval 0.0035 to 0.0082). Where both robots have fought before, Glicko-2 gains 0.0106 (0.0070 to 0.0136), 0.0086 more than where exactly one robot debuts (paired interval 0.0047 to 0.0125). The boundary, drawn after seeing the test fights, also holds in the calibration years and does not depend on the split year. That 0.0106 splits into three similar parts: an Elo rating with the official step beats the official score by 0.0039, raising the step from 35 to 48 adds 0.0034, and Glicko-2's uncertainty adds 0.0033. Above a predicted 0.8, the official favourite won 75% of 506 fights against 85% predicted on average.

title: What Do You Know and What Do I Know? A Configurational Study of Buyer and Supplier Capabilities, Interfirm Governance, and Supplier Performance
affiliations: Washington University in St. Louis, Aarhus University and University of Melbourne - Melbourne Business School

detail.title: What Do You Know and What Do I Know? A Configurational Study of Buyer and Supplier Capabilities, Interfirm Governance, and Supplier Performance

affiliations.org_name: University of Melbourne - Melbourne Business School
affiliations.preferred_name: University of Melbourne - Melbourne Business School

detail.abstract: Existing research on supplier performance examines governance, capabilities, and their pairwise interactions, but how they operate as complex, interdependent bundles remains unclear. We explore these configurations using Qualitative Comparative Analysis and Necessary Condition Analysis of survey data from the German machinery industry. Consistently high performance results from governance-capability fit. Capable buyers either use behavior monitoring and relational governance to compensate for weak supplier capabilities, or use output monitoring, relational governance, and supplier autonomy to leverage strong supplier capabilities. Output monitoring and relational governance constrain very high performance, suggesting each plays a more nuanced role than previously understood. These findings suggest a central role of governance in mobilizing capabilities, reveal asymmetries between buyer and supplier capabilities, and highlight the value of combining configurational and necessarycondition methods.

title: The Architecture of Governance Decay: A Longitudinal Analysis of Corruption, State Capture, and Institutional Vulnerabilities across ASEAN (2020-2025)

detail.title: The Architecture of Governance Decay: A Longitudinal Analysis of Corruption, State Capture, and Institutional Vulnerabilities across ASEAN (2020-2025)
detail.abstract: This research paper provides a comprehensive, longitudinal analysis of public sector corruption, state capture, and institutional governance dynamics across the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) from 2020 through 2025. Spanning a critical six-year period marked by the unprecedented socioeconomic disruptions of the COVID-19 pandemic, rapid digital economy acceleration, and intensified geopolitical rivalries, this study evaluates how systemic corruption evolved from localized transactional bribery into complex transnational networks. Anchored in Principal-Agent Theory and Collective Action Theory, the article examines the operational mechanisms of graft across ASEAN member states, highlighting the severe economic, social, and political costs imposed on regional integration. Through empirical data synthesized from global integrity frameworks, including Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI), the World Justice Project (WJP) Rule of Law Index, and World Bank governance indicators, the research assesses cross-cutting vulnerabilities such as the diversion of emergency relief funds, green energy climate finance leakage, opaque public procurement, and the role of professional financial gatekeepers in enabling illicit financial flows. Furthermore, the paper analyzes the systemic contraction of civic space, threats to whistleblowers, and judicial erosion that perpetuate systemic impunity across the region. Finally, the study offers actionable policy recommendations designed to strengthen regional anti-corruption mechanisms, enforce beneficial ownership transparency, protect civil society, and align the ASEAN Economic Community (AEC) with global governance standards.

title: Exponential Supermajority Escalator, a New Strategic Deterrent against Autocratic Entrenchment

detail.title: Exponential Supermajority Escalator, a New Strategic Deterrent against Autocratic Entrenchment

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author have no any conflict of interest concerning the submitted paper

publicationDetails.detailsText: It is submitted for pulication, not appeared as yet.

detail.abstract: Two decades of global democratic recession, often due to incumbent leaders' autocratic entrenchment despite constitutional term limits, call for innovating safeguards against autocratisation. The paper introduces a groundbreaking mechanism-the exponential supermajority thresholds escalator-which will diminish incumbents' growing advantage in reelection races by stipulating re-election on passing exponentially escalating supermajority thresholds. Drawing on vast literature and historical cases, the paper proposes stipulating additional office terms on passing exponential escalating supermajority thresholds (e.g., 2nd term~57% → 66.6% → 75% → 90%), creating a strategic incentive for leaders to abide by this democratic mechanism rather than opting for autocratic entrenchment. This mechanism can be adapted to both presidential and parliamentarian contexts; it proposes leaders' rotation that bars arbitrary removal of effective voter-serving transformative leaders. Against sceptics, the escalator's rising-bar logic amplifies resistance to subversion; it invites researchers, policymakers and constitutional designers to explore and test this promising safeguard against democratic erosion.

detail.abstract: This conceptual paper examines seven economic issues: inflation, interest, banking instability, financial bubbles, credit-inflated demand, public and private debt, and tax evasion in relation to fiscal stability. It explores a hypothetical economic architecture based on a common physical measure of economic value that could also serve as a unit of exchange; the separate recording of production, distribution, and market activity; full backing of transaction deposits; investment financed through existing funds; interest-free installment payments; and automatic taxation of final sales of newly produced goods and services. The proposals are considered in relation to established monetary and institutional mechanisms. The paper does not presume that these arrangements would eliminate inflation, financial crises, or fiscal deficits. Their feasibility requires accounting foundations, institutional design, and empirical testing.

title: Sub-fill Fragmentation in Real-Time Futures Feeds: Microstructure Distortion and Causal Consolidation for Event-driven Trading Systems

detail.title: Sub-fill Fragmentation in Real-Time Futures Feeds: Microstructure Distortion and Causal Consolidation for Event-driven Trading Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that he has no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. It was funded internally by QuantX Research (VectraQuant).

detail.abstract: Quantitative trading pipelines are routinely calibrated and validated offline on canonical institutional tick archives-such as CME Globex Market Data Platform (MDP 3.0) Topof-Book and Trade (TBBO) records-before being deployed on commercial or brokerage real-time streaming APIs (e.g., dxFeed TimeAndSale WebSockets). While both data sources report identical aggregate traded volume, they differ fundamentally in how matching-engine executions are serialized: institutional archives report an aggressor order sweeping multiple resting limit orders at a single price level as a consolidated transaction, whereas real-time brokerage feeds broadcast a separate tick event for every counterparty partial sub-fill. We prove analytically and demonstrate empirically that this sub-fill fragmentation induces severe structural divergence in event-driven sampling operators (such as Dollar Imbalance Bars) and order-flow microstructure features. Using synchronized production recordings on E-mini S&P 500 futures (/ES, 2, 606, 704 raw streaming sub-fills matched against 1, 213, 370 canonical CME MDP 3.0 trades across a 17-hour trading session), we show that 38.26% of aggressor orders are fragmented into m r ≥ 2 sub-fills (up to m r = 63), accounting for 71.27% of all raw tick notifications and 71.11% of traded volume. Operating an adaptive Dollar Imbalance Bar (RA-DIB) sampler directly on the unconsolidated stream inflates event counts by 2.148×, compresses average trade size by-53.46%, accelerates perevent EWMA memory decay, inflates closed bar counts by +55.47%, underestimates intrabar Herfindahl-Hirschman concentration (HHI) by-42.94%, inflates directional taker run lengths by +171.70%, and destroys-76.66% of institutional block-flow detection (≥ $1.5M). We introduce an O(1)-memory causal state-machine consolidator keyed on (trade_id, p i , b i) that restores 99.955% event parity, 99.85% bar-count parity, 100.00% HHI parity, and 99.98% institutional block-flow recovery with zero lookahead latency.

title: Believers versus Skeptics: Experimentation in Public Good Provision
affiliations: Johns Hopkins University and Duke Kunshan University

detail.title: Believers versus Skeptics: Experimentation in Public Good Provision

declarations.declarationOfInterest: There is no conflict of interest to declare.

detail.abstract: Disagreement over collective efforts against crises can persist when successful prevention conceals whether the efforts were needed. We study a two-period public good game between believers and skeptics under passive experimentation, where contribution obscures information. Greater skepticism in one group lowers everyone's contribution but speeds learning. A mean-preserving spread in priors raises total contribution when a bad outcome is likely and contributions are mildly effective. Sufficiently divergent priors can even induce over-provision. Under active experimentation, where contribution generates information, greater skepticism can instead raise the other group's contribution. In both settings, observability of contribution slows learning.

title: Validating Mortgage Default Models Through a Regime Change: Evidence from 10.8 Million Freddie Mac Loans, 2020 to 2026
affiliations: University of the Cumberlands (formerly Cumberland College)

detail.title: Validating Mortgage Default Models Through a Regime Change: Evidence from 10.8 Million Freddie Mac Loans, 2020 to 2026

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. The study uses only de-identified loan-level data that Freddie Mac makes available for research and involves no human participants.

detail.abstract:
Credit default models are usually validated on data from one stable period but used through regime changes. This paper validates default models on 10.8 million Freddie Mac mortgages with first payments from 2020 to mid-2024 and performance through June 2026, a period that spans COVID-19 forbearance, a refinancing boom and a rise in note rates from 2.8% to 7.3%. Default is 90 or more days of delinquency or a credit event within 24 months, excluding delinquency that began under forbearance. All data-dependent steps were fitted inside training folds, and models built on 2020 to 2022 loans were tested on a held-out sample and on all 1.23 million loans from 2023 and 2024. An ensemble of logistic regression and gradient boosting ranked risk best, with a ROC AUC of 0.807 in time (95% BCa interval 0.799 to 0.816) and 0.815 out of time (0.811 to 0.817), a small but significant gain over logistic regression. Repeated stratified cross-validation gave the most stable estimates, LOOCV was twice as biased and 400 times slower, and none of eight resampling methods improved ranking or cost. Predicted risk tracked a 2.6-fold rise in default rates because the riskier borrower mix was visible at origination, yet a fixed review cutoff flagged 24% of later loans instead of 5%, and about four in ten flagged loans were unstable across bootstrap refits. Early prepayment explained much of the calibration error by vintage, and only 5% of defaults ended in a credit event, so realized losses did not justify declining applications. The findings support capacity based review thresholds, population stability monitoring and competing risks models of default and prepayment.

title: Deterministic 3D Spatial Safety Envelopes in 8 W Bare-Metal FPGA Silicon for FDA Section 515C Predetermined Change Control Plans in Autonomous Surgical Robotics

detail.title: Deterministic 3D Spatial Safety Envelopes in 8 W Bare-Metal FPGA Silicon for FDA Section 515C Predetermined Change Control Plans in Autonomous Surgical Robotics

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the Founder and Chief Architect of Oikonomia Architektur / Oikonomia BioPharma, which developed the proprietary FPGA RTL netlists encapsulated within the evaluated Amazon FPGA Images (agfi-0b55f06c15a385187 and agfi-037dec8eb7fe5504d). The author declares no other competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was independently funded by Oikonomia Architektur / Oikonomia BioPharma. No external grants, public funding, or third-party commercial sponsorships were received for this work.

detail.abstract: Background: Under Section 515C of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) and U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) guidance on Predetermined Change Control Plans (PCCPs) for artificial intelligence-enabled medical devices [1, 2], surgical robotics manufacturers may deploy post-market machine learning updates without filing a new 510(k) or Premarket Approval (PMA) supplement only if clinical safety envelopes remain strictly invariant. When trajectory planners and safety monitors co-reside on host CPUs or GPUs, software model updates risk introducing operating-system scheduling jitter, Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) coordinate mutations in shared DRAM, and non-deterministic floating-point drift. Methods: We verified a dual-bitstream bare-metal Xilinx UltraScale+ FPGA hardware safety architecture (0000:34:00.0 on AWS EC2 f2.6xlarge) operating at 8 W VCCINT steady-state core power (10 W peak) across direct userspace PCIe Gen3 x16 BAR0 MMIO. Bitstream agfi-0b55f06c15a385187 encodes a 16 × 16 × 16 (4,096-byte, 1.0 mm isotropic resolution) 3D skull-base neurovascular keep-out map (448 protected voxels spanning the internal carotid artery and optic nerve sheath) evaluated against 1,000 swept end-effector trajectory tensors. Bitstream agfi-037dec8eb7fe5504d enforces pre-actuation force, velocity, monotonic epoch, and cryptographic digest invariants across 10,000 actuator commands (5,000 compliant + 5,000 injected faults) coupled to a 21-cycle (84.0 ns) physical motor-torque drop shunt and a constant O(1) 256-byte bijective integer black-box recorder. Results: The bare-metal 3D voxel engine detected 500 of 500 (100.00%) anatomical keep-out incursions at 87.020 μs P50 (96.180 μs P99) latency—consuming <8.7% of a standard 1 kHz (1,000 μs) surgical servo control cycle—with 100% bit-exact register determinism. Across 10,000 actuator commands, the hardware gate blocked 5,000 of 5,000 (100.00%) fault trajectories (1,250 anatomical boundary breaches, 1,250 force/velocity overshoots, 1,250 TOCTOU DRAM coordinate mutations, and 1,250 stale command replays) at 150.00 ns P50 (260.00 ns P99) latency and an 84.0 ns physical drop shunt. Post-incident black-box unwinding across 1,000 trajectory steps within the 0.25 KB manifold achieved 0 bits of least-significant-bit (LSB) drift. Conclusions: Relocating 3D anatomical keep-out boundaries and pre-actuation motor cutoffs from mutable host AI software into deterministic, 8 W bare-metal FPGA silicon provides a hardware-invariant safety boundary aligned with FDA Section 515C PCCP verification requirements.

title: An Efficient and Explainable Hybrid Machine Learning Framework for Heart Disease Risk Classification

detail.title: An Efficient and Explainable Hybrid Machine Learning Framework for Heart Disease Risk Classification

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The research was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: Heart disease risk classification from routine clinical attributes is a common machine-learning benchmark, yet reported accuracies are often inflated by duplicated records and by preprocessing that leaks test information. This paper evaluates a lightweight, explainable hybrid framework on the public Kaggle "Heart Disease" table (1,025 rows). We find that 723 rows (70.5%) are exact duplicates of 302 unique records; a naive split would place an identical copy of 98.5% of test rows in the training set. After de-duplication we use a stratified 80:20 split (241/61), and perform scaling, feature selection (SelectKBest) and hyper-parameter tuning only inside cross-validation on the training data. Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting (GB) and an equal-weight soft-voting hybrid of the three are compared on accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, Brier score, training time, inference time and model size, with bootstrap confidence intervals. On the held-out test set, LR scored highest (accuracy 0.836, AUC 0.903) and the hybrid did not outperform it (accuracy 0.803, AUC 0.887); all differences lie well inside the bootstrap uncertainty of a 61-patient test set. Over 20 repeated stratified hold-out splits the hybrid had the highest mean AUC (0.915 ± 0.029) but its margin over RF was negligible (+0.0001) and over LR small (+0.007). The hybrid cost about 27× the training time and 270× the model size of LR. Shapley-value and LIME-style explanations agree that chest-pain type, number of major vessels, thalassemia status and maximum heart rate dominate predictions. The study is a methodological comparison on a small public dataset and is not a clinically validated diagnostic system.

detail.abstract: The implementation of brand and consumer loyalty strategies impacts the financial standing of an organisation. Toyota, one of the Japanese automotive manufacturers, maintains the sustainability of its brand internationally by implementing a marketing strategy based on a collectivist cultural approach. In the context of Toyota's marketing strategy, this article offers an analysis of contemporary marketing strategies. The research employed a literature review approach, which allowed for the identification of prospective areas that warrant further investigation. This paper presents an integration of Toyota's marketing strategy, the current marketing strategy, and the traditional marketing mix model. Effective communication and marketing strategies implemented by Toyota have been identified as a critical factor in the company's sustained market position, according to the study. The article discusses the performance and strategy of marketing, as well as the theoretical, research, and practical implications. Additional research is required in order to enhance the applicability of these results.

title: CRAB-H: Task-Centric Certification for Healthcare Autonomous Systems
affiliations: Navigator Global LLC and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: CRAB-H: Task-Centric Certification for Healthcare Autonomous Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors are respectively chairman of the board of Wybe labs Inc and employed at Wybe Robotics AS.

affiliations.org_name: Unaffiliated Authors - affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.abstract: This paper introduces CRAB-H as a task-centric certification methodology for healthcare autonomous systems. CRAB-H extends the ARC governance architecture [1] by introducing the task as a first-class governance object, represented through Task Requirement Profiles (TRP-H). Each profile defines the cognitive capabilities, governance constraints, evidentiary requirements, and operational assumptions necessary for the safe execution of a specific healthcare activity. Rather than asking whether a robot achieves a sufficiently high benchmark score, CRAB-H asks whether demonstrated capabilities satisfy the requirements of the task. Certification becomes a comparison between demonstrated capability and required capability. A reliability-gated assurance allocation mechanism routes cognitive dimensions that cannot be reproducibly evaluated to LEA operational requirements rather than discarding them. Governance integrity is preserved: unreliable dimensions are governed, not ignored. The Capability Margin is defined as the threshold-based conjunction of per-dimension compliance determinations, not as a subtracted scalar-preserving non-compensatory governance logic appropriate for safety-critical healthcare deployment. Terminology Note The term CRAB-H was used in earlier working documents to refer to the broader healthcare domain suite of CRAB evaluation dimensions. This paper establishes CRAB-H as the task-centric certification methodology for healthcare autonomous systems-a structured approach to representing task cognitive requirements as governance objects. Earlier working document references to CRAB-H as a domain suite will be updated to align with this canonical definition. ARC-1 [1] domain references will be revised accordingly in subsequent versions.

detail.abstract: We evaluate the effect of Mozambique's 2019 Tuberculosis Preventive Treatment (TPT) Guidelines, centered on the 3HP regimen (isoniazid plus rifapentine) and the levofloxacin protocol for contacts of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) patients, on tuberculosis prevalence. We build a balanced panel of Mozambique's 11 provinces over 2010-2024 (165 observations) from administrative records of the Ministry of Health (MISAU), the National Statistics Institute (INE), and the World Health Organization (WHO). Our specification is a difference-indifferences (DiD) design with province and year fixed effects (TWFE), comparing the four southern provinces that adopted the Guidelines in 2019 (Maputo City, Maputo Province, Gaza, and Inhambane) with the remaining seven. Controlling for socioeconomic and structural covariates, we estimate a treatment effect of-0.448 (p < 0.001) on log notified cases, an implied reduction of about 36%. We then stress-test this result. An event study shows the effect emerges only from the second post-treatment year, yet a parallel-trends pre-test is rejected. As a robustness check, we apply the Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021) estimator, which relaxes strict parallel trends and is robust to dynamic treatment-effect heterogeneity; it yields an ATT of-0.098, statistically zero (p = 0.346). A Rambachan and Roth (2023) sensitivity analysis confirms that the post-treatment effect remains insignificant under any plausible deviation from parallel trends. We conclude that much of the headline coefficient likely reflects divergent pre-2019 trajectories between southern and other provinces, and we therefore urge caution in interpreting its magnitude.

detail.abstract: AI data centers collect operational events, evaluate system behavior, and sometimes publish claims about reliability. A reported decline in failures can reflect improved performance, a change in the types of cases measured, or weakened detection. This working paper proposes a thirteen-article constitution for AI data centers that turns Faithful Intelligence commitments into evidence rules, decision rights, and auditable controls. This paper is part of the Faithful Intelligence Series. It extends the program's verification architecture to the governance of AI data centers. A purposive documentary review compares the proposed obligations against three public governance and risk-management documents from NIST and the OECD and uses a previously posted operational research constitution as a methodological precedent. The review finds documentary alignment on oversight, evaluation, and incident management. It also identifies design choices that require local implementation, including rules for adjudicating conflicting sources, preserving trial denominators, and authorizing publication and research use. A synthetic accounting example demonstrates how the same response records can support distinct quality and delivery estimates. A proposed paired evaluation would test whether the controls improve source fidelity and detection without unacceptable losses in answer coverage. The review identifies design correspondences and testable propositions within the selected corpus. Live operating performance and causal effects await empirical evaluation.
